title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI image generation system was used to create non-consensual sexual abuse material of a real person. The attacker obtained photographs from the victim's private social media, used them as input to an AI model to generate explicit content, then distributed the output across multiple platforms under fake identities. It is not established whether the AI system had any safeguards against this use, or what those safeguards were.

The deployment failure was at the point of distribution rather than generation. The attacker used multiple fake accounts, email addresses, and platforms to evade detection and hide his identity. Catching this would have required either the AI platform to restrict non-consensual intimate imagery at the point of creation, the social platforms to detect and prevent distribution of such content, or both. The fact that other unknown users created additional images and reposted them after the initial upload shows the content spread beyond the original attacker.

It is not established what technical or policy measures, if any, were in place to prevent or detect the creation or sharing of non-consensual intimate images on the systems involved.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and distributing sexually explicit artificial intelligence-generated images of a college acquaintance. Bansal obtained photographs from the woman's private social media account and used AI technology to create obscene morphed images. He then circulated this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using several Gmail addresses to hide his identity. The woman discovered the abuse when she received messages from anonymous accounts informing her that her morphed photographs and videos were being shared on Discord servers, along with threatening messages designed to humiliate and harass her.

Police launched an investigation after the 22-year-old victim reported the crime to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi. Investigators analyzed digital footprints and traced connections between the fake social media accounts and email addresses. Bansal was eventually identified and arrested. During questioning, he admitted that he knew the victim from college and had harbored personal resentment toward her following repeated insults. He also disclosed that after uploading the initial content, other unknown users created additional explicit images and videos, which he subsequently reposted. Police recovered his mobile phone, two SIM cards, and other relevant digital evidence as the investigation continues.
title_en: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online
